text:
morgan: Heads-up: in the latest dashboard build the left axis uses full labels and pushes the plot area. Proposing a "signpost" approach: show compact numeric ticks + a small unit signpost (pill) that is keyboard-focusable and reveals the full axis label + aggregation on focus. Thoughts?

harpreet: +1. Signpost keeps ticks clean. Can we make the pill context-aware so it moves into the legend area on narrow widths? Avoid overlaying series.

sylvie: UX nit: call the pill "Unit" not "Units" to match other UI. Also include a micro hint below: e.g. "Unit: req/s (1m avg)" in lighter text.

noah: Implementation: if we keep ticks as plain numbers we must ensure abbrev rules are consistent. Abbrev only when >=1000 (k, M). Avoid decimals like 0.45k. Also preserve minus sign next to number.

aria: Accessibility: critical points:
- pill must be focusable (tabindex=0) with aria-expanded on the explainer
- axis container must have aria-label with the full phrase like "Requests per second, unit: req/s"
- ticks should provide aria-valuetext so SR reads full value including unit
- do NOT hide full label with display:none for SRs
Also add an optional aria-live region that can announce extreme spikes when they are de-emphasized.

morgan: Outlier handling: debating between soft-dim (alpha) vs top-cap marker. Soft-dim is cheap and preserves scale; caps make it explicit but risk being mistaken for annotations. Preference for soft-dim with configurable threshold.

harpreet: Agreed soft-dim first. Suggest knee threshold so only very large deviations get de-emphasized; small-but-still-large peaks should remain visible.

sylvie: Copy: call the setting "De-emphasize extreme values (visual only)" not "hide outliers". Tooltip: "Values are visually de-emphasized; data is preserved and available on hover."

noah: Smoothing: default OFF for dashboard timeseries. For microcharts (sparklines) default ON. Implementation idea: apply smoothing as a visual overlay only; hover tooltips still show raw points. That avoids changing underlying data.

morgan: Quick CSS hint for signpost float -> legend flow:
```css
.chart__unit-signpost{position:absolute;right:12px;top:8px;padding:4px 8px;border-radius:8px;background:#ffffff;border:1px solid #e6e8eb}
@media(max-width:420px){.chart__unit-signpost{position:static;margin-left:8px}}
```

harpreet: Perf: soft-dim is cheap in canvas. If we later add cap markers or density indicators, prefer a single overlay canvas layer for markers to avoid many DOM nodes.

sylvie: Test plan: prototype two variants: A) signpost + soft-dim, B) inline abbr + cap markers. Recruit 6 participants (4 engineers, 2 PMs) with tasks: "Locate the largest spike in last 24h" and "Read the unit for the left axis using keyboard only." Measure time-to-task + confidence. Also include 1 screen-reader tester.

aria: A11y checklist to include with prototype:
- signpost has role=button + aria-expanded and an explainer region referenced by aria-describedby
- axis group has aria-label with full unit + aggregation window
- ticks expose aria-valuetext with localized number + unit
- smoothing toggle uses aria-pressed and updates accessible label when toggled
- optional aria-live announcements for de-emphasized spikes with setting to opt-out

noah: Minor: when using abbreviation, ensure tooltip shows the full expanded number on hover/focus, not the abbrev. Eg tooltip should show "1,200" not "1.2k".

morgan: OK let's build A+B mocks. Kai, can you mock desktop + mobile states? I'll assemble test plan and copy options. We'll reconvene Fri. :thumbsup:

ux-bot: New mock requested: chart unit signpost variants. Link placeholder: https://redwood-inference.design/mocks/signpost-variants-2026-03-23.png :frame_with_picture:
